_about: Edge cases a good test list for each ticket must contain, graded by `npm run eval:edges` against whatever testcases.json each ticket's run holds now. A judge model decides, per edge, which case (if any) exercises it; an edge no case exercises is a missing edge case. Edges marked `source: bug` are real defects found in that run by verify or review, so a list without them provably let a bug through; `source: ticket` edges come from the ticket's own scope. Re-run the testcases phase on a ticket after a prompt change, then run the eval, to see whether the change made the lists weaker. `project` is the GitLab project the iids belong to.

8772.edge: A People Report amount with a long float tail (API 145635.25999999998) renders as 145,635.26, with no comma inside the decimals.
A small amount with a float tail (API 78.00000000000001) renders as 78.00, keeping two decimal places.
An amount over a million (API 1460414.8599999999) is grouped every three digits in the whole-number part only and renders as 1,460,414.86.
An amount of exactly zero renders as 0.00 on the People Report.
A negative amount keeps its minus sign and is grouped in the whole-number part only.
The People Report CSV export writes every Amount with at most two decimal places, matching the table.
Profile Entitlements, which shares the number formatter, shows its figures without a comma inside the decimals and with the same digits as before.
Person Equity, which shares the number formatter, shows its figures without a comma inside the decimals, keeping every decimal it had and its currency prefix.
The Payroll Dashboard financial summary, which shares the number formatter, keeps its existing money formatting with no comma inside the decimals.

8781.edge: A recreational-trip claim with 4 participants reimbursed at an Amount Paid of 44,000 records exactly 11,000 against each participant.
An Amount Paid that does not divide evenly across participants is split so the active rows total it exactly to the cent and never exceed it.
Submitting a trip claim creates exactly one expense-person row per participant, with no inactive duplicate rows at 0.00.
A global-subcontractor participant stays at 0.00 and is left out of the divisor, so the eligible participants split the whole Amount Paid.
Reimbursing several trip claims in one bulk decision apportions each claim from its own Amount Paid.
A bulk reimbursement whose request body sends status as the string "3" instead of the integer 3 still apportions the Amount Paid to the per-person rows.
An Official Trip claim is reimbursed without the equal-share apportionment touching its participants' rows.
